file_contents: This OCR file holds BOTH parts of AA 1: pars prior (Salvianus, ed. C. Halm, 1877; lines 1-14590) and pars posterior (Eugippius, Vita S. Severini, ed. H. Sauppe, 1877; lines 14600-18547). Victor Vitensis is NOT in AA 1; it is AA 3 pars prior.

texts.work: Salvianus, De gubernatione dei libri VIII

sigla.manuscript: second (correcting) hand in A, called 'emendatrix sive potius corruptrix'

evidence.quote: Is cum in multis optimis lectionibus cum Corbeiensi conspiret, primo aspectu ex ipso eum descriptum esse suspicere, sed rem non ita se habere ex compluribus lacunis ... apparet
Eundem codicem aut saltem eius simillimum Pithoeo ... praesto fuisse cum ex aliis locis elucet
Ex quo codice editio princeps, a. 1530 cura Io. Alexandri Brassicani vulgata, expressa sit, ignoratur.

texts.notes: Halm only says A is the best and oldest, B comes next and is not a copy of A (B alone has true readings in some places), and Pithou's lost codex was B or close to it. No grouping of A, B, T into families is stated; T is described but not placed.

sigla.manuscript: first hand vs correction in B

evidence.quote: nobis quidem manifestum videtur, hunc librum ... ex nullo alio originem duxisse nisi ex ipso Parisino n. 2785
Nos praeter codicem n. 2785 alterum Parisinum n. 2172, saeculo fere vetustiorem, quo iam Pithoeus videtur usus esse, contulimus.

texts.notes: The only filiation statement eliminates Baluze's 'recentior' codex as a copy of Paris. 2785 (not used). No relation between A, B and Sichard's source is stated. Only 2 manuscripts plus an early edition, so it will fail the 4-witness rule anyway.

texts.work: Eugippius, Vita S. Severini (with Epistola ad Paschasium and Paschasii epistola)

sigla.manuscript: Monacensis lat. (four leaves; OCR reads 'cod. lat. 104r', probably clm 1044), covers ep. and c. 1-4, 14-22 only
a slightly later hand in L ('manus haud multo recentior nonnulla mutavit')
Anonymus Valesianus, excerpt of c. 7 / c. 32 (testimonium, no siglum in the apparatus list)

evidence.quote: Videtur igitur ita existimandum esse, ut codices L et VM ex duobus apographis unius archetypi ... derivandos esse iudicemus, quorum alterum, ex quo L originem duxit, maiore fide descriptum esset
in aliis ab eo ita discrepant, ut alius originis indicia habeant et pauca quaedam emendatiora et pleniora exhibeant, quam lateranensis et reliqui omnes
eis foliis magis cum codicibus VM quam cum L convenire, propius etiam ad similitudinem eius accedere, ex quo welseriana expressa est
Quae omnia quamquam L accuratius quam VM, satis propinqua illos cum eo cognatione coniunctos ... ostendunt

texts.notes: The two-apograph statement (L vs VM) is explicit. D is placed only as 'agreeing more with VM than with L' and as belonging to the corrupt Munich recension, so putting D in the VM branch is my reading; it is a fragment. One aside (p. XIII, line 15003) speaks of a 'commune codicum LM archetypum' for a single error, which an editor-reader should check. The c. 30 other MSS (Bethmann's collations) are deliberately not reported.

skipped.reason: single manuscript (one codex s. X, split between Bern and Paris. 3791, siglum C)
fragment of 1 page; three Paris MSS cited (num. 11560 s. VII-VIII = A, two others s. IX-X = B, C), no filiation stated
one manuscript (Paris. 2785) plus Sichard's edition; c. 3 pages, no filiation
